Even after maintenance checked it, it’s still bringing in cold air and now we can barely open and close the entrance door. The common kitchen has barely any equipment and people steal constantly. Maybe use locks and a rental system/mandatory payment for new kitchen equipment which is locked and tracked, or worst case cameras (we did that in a previous dorm). People also generally don’t clean after themselves in the community areas. Lastly, having two (!!) vacuums for the whole village of 360 villagers is just unreasonable. Also because they keep being gone for way longer than 1h and often I find both in the same laundromat. Might make sense to just paint it according to the colour. Lastly, I know the washing machines are handled by a third party service, but the prices are outrageous. I have a dust allergy so I need to wash ca twice a week, and I can’t even add my laundry disinfectant, the “allergy” washing cycle doesn’t help either. Generally not the greatest living environment if I’m being honest, there’s much better places for the total price (considering needing to buy your own vacuum, own ladder, laundry prices and constantly rebuying kitchen appliances bc they’ve been stolen in the kitchen). Otherwise it’s a super nice idea of having a real community, and I understand some things are out of your hands. But hopefully you can implement some of these suggestions:)) | Måned: Nov | År: 2025 | Landsby: Nørrebro | Kildeark: Nov 2025

nodes.combined_text:
Spørgsmål: Last step! Is there anything else you'd like to tell us? 🌿 | Svar: It would be awesome to have a proper workshop space in the village—especially for things like woodworking and bike repairs. A lot of us try to build our own furniture or fix our bikes, but right now it's pretty tricky. We're either using super basic tools that aren’t really up to the job, or we have to rent expensive tools from places like Sylvan. On top of that, there's no real workspace, which makes things slow, a bit unsafe, and honestly kind of frustrating.
 
 Having a shared workshop with decent tools would make a big difference. It would give people the chance to actually work on projects—either alone or together—and make our rooms and the village better overall. Especially for international students who don’t bring all their tools with them, this would be super helpful. Right now, the lack of resources kind of holds people back from putting in the effort, even if they’re motivated.
 
 A workshop would not only support creativity and practical skills, but it would also make the rent feel more worthwhile. We’re already trying to make the most out of small spaces, and often the best solutions are the ones we build ourselves—if we had the chance.
 
 To keep the tools secure—especially the more expensive ones—a locking system using our existing electronic key system could work well. Since the keys already have electronic signatures, it should be possible to track who last accessed the workshop or used specific tools. That way, if anything goes missing or gets damaged, it’s easier to follow up responsibly.
 
 **Suggestion for the Village: Furniture Reuse Corner + Swapping Platform**
 
 Additionally, it would be great to have a dedicated space where people who are leaving can place their furniture or useful items in a dry, safe, and organized way instead of just tossing them next to the trash. Right now, a lot of perfectly good furniture gets ruined by the weather and ends up going to waste, which is a shame. Many of us could make use of these things, and it would save a lot of money and resources.
 
 One possible location could be one of the covered niches near the containers, on the side without staircases. That area already has three walls and a roof, so it wouldn’t take much to turn it into a reuse corner. To keep it organized, there could be a simple set of rules—for example, items should be tied together if disassembled, and a photo showing how it looks assembled should be included.
 
 An additional idea that could make this even more effective would be to create a simple item-swapping platform or bulletin board, where people who are leaving can post things they want to give away, and incoming residents (added once they sign a rental contract) can express interest. That way, items would only be left behind if someone actually wants them. It would also keep the reuse area cleaner and prevent it from becoming a dumping zone for unwanted stuff. Right now, it's hard to connect with future tenants due to the lack of overlap, so something like this could really help bridge that gap.
 
 Just like with the workshop, the reuse area could also be secured using the electronic key system to keep things safe and organized. A camera would to it as well...
 
 And then another point: | Måned: May | År: 2025 | Landsby: Nørrebro | Kildeark: May 2025

nodes.combined_text: Spørgsmål: Last step! Is there anything else you'd like to tell us? 🌿 | Svar: Jeg synes, at village vesterbro er et dejligt sted at bo, i sær med udearealerne. Jeg synes, at værelset kan blive rigtig varmt om sommeren (også med vinduet åbnet) og rigtig koldt om vinteren. Når køleskabet i køkkenet er placeret op af væggen, så er det svært at åbne fryseren, fordi køleskabsdøren går ind i væggen. Så det kunne have været rart hvis, man havde tænkt over funktionalitet, når man placerede køleskabet. Derudover synes jeg ventilationsystemet på badeværelset ofte går igang senere, når man er i bad, hvilket gør badeværelset meget fugtigt. Gangen er ret mørk, og kold om vinteren. Jeg synes at vaskemaskiner er ret små i forhold til hvor meget man skal vaske, så det kunne have været med to (eller en) store vaskemaskiner og to små. Ellers synes jeg fælleshuset har fået et flot interiør og en masse godt køkkengrej, så man har lyst til at opholde og lave mad der. | Måned: May | År: 2025 | Landsby: Vesterbro | Kildeark: May 2025

Når køleskabet i køkkenet er placeret op af væggen, så er det svært at åbne fryseren, fordi køleskabsdøren går ind i væggen. Så det kunne have været rart hvis, man havde tænkt over funktionalitet, når man placerede køleskabet. Derudover synes jeg ventilationsystemet på badeværelset ofte går igang senere, når man er i bad, hvilket gør badeværelset meget fugtigt. Gangen er ret mørk, og kold om vinteren. nodes.combined_text: Spørgsmål: Optional - why did you give your apartment this rating? 🛋️ | Svar: I rated the apartment 7/10 mainly because I genuinely appreciate many aspects of the place, especially its location, layout, and day-to-day functionality. The area is very convenient and well-connected, which makes living here practical and comfortable. I like that I have easy access to transportation, shops, and different services, so I don’t need to spend extra time on basic errands or commuting. The surrounding neighborhood feels pleasant, reasonably quiet, and generally safe, and I enjoy the atmosphere here — it strikes a nice balance between calm and urban convenience. This was one of the strongest factors influencing my score. I also value the functionality of the apartment itself. The space is laid out in a way that makes everyday living smooth and efficient. It’s easy to organize the rooms, move around, cook, rest, and work without feeling restricted. I appreciate that the apartment has what I need on a daily basis, and the interior feels practical and comfortable enough to spend time in. It’s definitely a place where I can settle into a routine without too much effort, which is something I consider important. At the same time, the reason I didn’t give a higher rating is because I believe there are still a few areas that could be improved or refined to make the space feel even better. Although I’m overall happy with the experience, I think with small upgrades or improvements — whether related to comfort, equipment, design, or general upkeep — the apartment could easily become even more enjoyable to live in. My rating reflects the balance of positive qualities and a bit of room for enhancement. So overall, I am satisfied and have had a good experience living here, mainly because of the location, practicality, and general usability of the apartment. I gave it a 7/10 because it meets my needs well, but I also see potential for it to become even better with some adjustments or improvements. | Måned: Nov | År: 2025 | Landsby: Østerbro | Kildeark: Nov 2025

nodes.combined_text:
Spørgsmål: Last step! Is there anything else you'd like to tell us? 🌿 | Svar: In general I think improvements could be made as to how comfortable the common areas are. The mattresses on the benches in the kitchen could fx be made to fit the bench/window sill, as they slide around and sometimes you have to sit half on a pillow half on the bench. Also the table height doesn't really match the bench nor the chairs comfortably. 
 For the living room part; when we have movie nights in yellow, there isn't enough room for everyone in the two sofas, which means if you're unlucky you might have to sit on a regular chair for the entire movie. I think it could be great if we could fit in three sofas, and some that are maybe more comfortable than the ones we have, as we have the same issues with the mattresses on the sofa as the mattresses in the kitchen. They don't fit well enough and slide around, which means the sofas aren't really that comfortable. Maybe it could just be an option with better (and bigger) mattresses that actually fits the sofa and that are stuck. Lastly, sometimes it's difficult to enjoy a movie when a lot of people are talking/cooking/listening to music in the kitchen at the same time. Me and a few other villagers have discussed the possibility of installing some "heavy" and "kind-of-soundproofing" curtains between the two rooms to block out a bit of the noise. 
 Otherwise all in all im very happy with living in the village :) | Måned: May | År: 2025 | Landsby: Nørrebro | Kildeark: May 2025
nodes.Answer:
In general I think improvements could be made as to how comfortable the common areas are. The mattresses on the benches in the kitchen could fx be made to fit the bench/window sill, as they slide around and sometimes you have to sit half on a pillow half on the bench. Also the table height doesn't really match the bench nor the chairs comfortably. 
 For the living room part; when we have movie nights in yellow, there isn't enough room for everyone in the two sofas, which means if you're unlucky you might have to sit on a regular chair for the entire movie. I think it could be great if we could fit in three sofas, and some that are maybe more comfortable than the ones we have, as we have the same issues with the mattresses on the sofa as the mattresses in the kitchen. They don't fit well enough and slide around, which means the sofas aren't really that comfortable. Maybe it could just be an option with better (and bigger) mattresses that actually fits the sofa and that are stuck. Lastly, sometimes it's difficult to enjoy a movie when a lot of people are talking/cooking/listening to music in the kitchen at the same time. Me and a few other villagers have discussed the possibility of installing some "heavy" and "kind-of-soundproofing" curtains between the two rooms to block out a bit of the noise. 
 Otherwise all in all im very happy with living in the village :)

Is there anything else you'd like to tell us? 🌿 | Svar: Including housing subsidies in the presented rent price creates a misleading impression of affordability, as it masks the true cost of housing. Rent should reflect the actual price landlords are charging for the space, not an artificially reduced figure based on government assistance. Housing subsidies are government funds designed to support individuals, and should not be factored into rent prices since they are independent of the landlord’s pricing. The core issue is that rent in general is far too high considering the actual sizes of the rooms, and such practices only obscure the reality of unaffordable housing, making it harder for people to understand the true financial burden, they are facing. | Måned: May | År: 2025 | Landsby: Refshaleøen | Kildeark: May 2025
nodes.Answer: Including housing subsidies in the presented rent price creates a misleading impression of affordability, as it masks the true cost of housing. Rent should reflect the actual price landlords are charging for the space, not an artificially reduced figure based on government assistance. Housing subsidies are government funds designed to support individuals, and should not be factored into rent prices since they are independent of the landlord’s pricing. The core issue is that rent in general is far too high considering the actual sizes of the rooms, and such practices only obscure the reality of unaffordable housing, making it harder for people to understand the true financial burden, they are facing.

nodes.label: n000703
nodes.combined_text: Spørgsmål: Help us understand what works! *Comments or thoughts on the shared village spaces? 🌱* | Svar: I have generally positive thoughts about the shared village spaces, and I really appreciate how functional and comfortable they are to use. The layout is well-designed, practical, and makes it easy to sit down with a laptop to work, relax with friends, or cook and prepare meals. Cooking here is surprisingly enjoyable, and the open setup creates a very social and welcoming atmosphere. I also really like the overall design — the colors, the layout, the furniture and decorations — everything feels modern, friendly and pleasant to spend time in. One of the biggest advantages for me is the atmosphere of the space, with games and common areas that make it easy to connect with others, hang out, and enjoy time together. It’s definitely one of the things that makes the village feel alive and community-driven. However, I sometimes notice issues related more to how people use the space rather than the space itself. After bigger gatherings or parties the shared areas can get quite dirty, and fairly often I find myself cleaning up after others to make the place comfortable to use again. It’s not really a fault of the village, but it does impact the experience. Another challenge is the limited number of laundry baskets and kitchen items — many people take them to their rooms and don’t return them, which means there are fewer available for everyone else. It would be helpful to have more baskets or a system that encourages items to be returned after use. The same happens sometimes with dishes and utensils, so increasing the quantity could balance this problem. In general, I love the idea of the shared spaces — the functionality, the atmosphere, the possibility to work, cook, socialize or simply relax. The space itself works extremely well, and I enjoy spending time there. The main issues come from how some people treat it rather than from the space itself, and with a bit more responsibility or more shared items available, the experience could be even better. Overall, I think the shared village areas are a strong part of the community and a place with great potential, and I genuinely appreciate being able to use them. | Måned: Nov | År: 2025 | Landsby: Østerbro | Kildeark: Nov 2025

Another challenge is the limited number of laundry baskets and kitchen items — many people take them to their rooms and don’t return them, which means there are fewer available for everyone else. It would be helpful to have more baskets or a system that encourages items to be returned after use. The same happens sometimes with dishes and utensils, so increasing the quantity could balance this problem. In general, I love the idea of the shared spaces — the functionality, the atmosphere, the possibility to work, cook, socialize or simply relax. The space itself works extremely well, and I enjoy spending time there. The main issues come from how some people treat it rather than from the space itself, and with a bit more responsibility or more shared items available, the experience could be even better. Overall, I think the shared village areas are a strong part of the community and a place with great potential, and I genuinely appreciate being able to use them.

nodes.combined_text:
Spørgsmål: Is there something that could improve your social experience in the village? | Svar: I believe upgrading the Orangerie further would strongly improve the social experience.
 
 In winter/early spring the orangerie gets quite cold - and, i've been told, we are not allowed to heat it up with an electric heater (maybe due to a fire hazard?) - we have some blankets but its not really enough. If we would be able to heat uo the orangerie more socialising could be facilitated. 
 
 Also if the noise of the street could be dimmed by noise insulation material - people would stay longer and have a greater time there. 
 
 As it is the sole room in which more than 5 people can comfortably get together this could be worth the investment to facilitate social engagements. | Måned: May | År: 2025 | Landsby: Amagerbro | Kildeark: May 2025

nodes.combined_text: Spørgsmål: Optional - why did you give your apartment this rating? 🛋️ | Svar: I really thought about each question, so even though I rate everything at 8, it is my true feeling. I'm super happy about CPH Village in general - the rent is lower than most, I have a lovely neighbour, it's fairly easy for me to get to school (DTU), and everything is new. There are only a few reasons I don't give things a 10. For example, the air conditioning is non-existent in the corridor, extremely loud in our rooms, and weak in the bathroom. Every day now that it's winter, the windows are so wet on the outside that I cannot see out of them. And something else, is that I left some food (bread and cheese) in the common freezer the other day, only for a couple of weeks (clearly sealed, marked and everything) and it was stolen :( That gave me a bad feeling in my stomach. But to end on a positive note - I am extremely grateful to have found CPHV and gotten an apartment there. | Måned: Nov | År: 2025 | Landsby: Østerbro | Kildeark: Nov 2025

nodes.combined_text:
Spørgsmål: Last step! Is there anything else you'd like to tell us? 🌿 | Svar: The new booking system really isn’t ideal. People often end up double-booking time slots, and it’s frustrating that you can’t see who made the other booking to contact them directly. That means someone from the village office always has to step in as a middleman, which takes more time and just adds unnecessary stress to the whole process since it's hard to know how many people the other person is planning to invite, or if there might be any issues with overlapping events.
 
 Also, I brought this up a few months ago, but nothing has been done - the ramp to the disabled apartments is still really slippery when wet, which seems unsafe, and no measures have been taken. It would also be great to add stairs at the opposite end of the ramp. People are always jumping over the fence there, which not only looks dangerous, especially when it’s been raining, but can also cause a lot of noise that startles the people living next to it. | Måned: May | År: 2025 | Landsby: Vesterbro | Kildeark: May 2025
nodes.Answer:
The new booking system really isn’t ideal. People often end up double-booking time slots, and it’s frustrating that you can’t see who made the other booking to contact them directly. That means someone from the village office always has to step in as a middleman, which takes more time and just adds unnecessary stress to the whole process since it's hard to know how many people the other person is planning to invite, or if there might be any issues with overlapping events.
 
 Also, I brought this up a few months ago, but nothing has been done - the ramp to the disabled apartments is still really slippery when wet, which seems unsafe, and no measures have been taken. It would also be great to add stairs at the opposite end of the ramp. People are always jumping over the fence there, which not only looks dangerous, especially when it’s been raining, but can also cause a lot of noise that startles the people living next to it.

Is there anything else you'd like to tell us? 🌿 | Svar: The only thing that always surprises me (because all other things are so well organized and student-minded) is that to me, the “fine” for making holes in the wall is so much money, which to me a bit over the top. Friends have had to throw out curtains and everything, just because they needed to deliver the room white and without holes in the walls, and then the new person would buy new curtains (sometimes the exact same) again. That is a waste of money and resources, especially since students are generally very willing to take over others stuff (even more in the “sustainable living” culture like this village). Some friends had to pay insane amounts even though the walls were clean and white. It prevents me also from hanging anything on the walls, whereas in a small space like ours it can be super beneficial to use the space on the walls for storage or decoration. It would be great if there was a better system for easy and accessible contact with the person who takes over your room, to discuss and agree on having things on the walls (or holes/screws in the walls). Especially keeping in mind that 2000 dkk for 1 wall is a lot of money for a student. Other than that, I love the village and I think it’s an amazing place to live with a lot of great opportunities to meet people and live sustainably!! :) | Måned: May | År: 2025 | Landsby: Vesterbro | Kildeark: May 2025

Spørgsmål: Last question! Is there anything else you'd like to tell us? 🌿 | Svar: When I moved in I didn’t know what the “rules” were for the community/ social gatherings. I got the impression that there where groups people where hanging in, and that it was hard to know about the small events. or messenger groups where people planned events but they weren’t shared in the big group. Suddenly I’d walk past a big put lock dinner that I hadn’t heard of, which left me feeling uninvited. I have slowly found my way, but perhaps some other event on top of board game nights to include people when they move in, could be an idea. So that people feel involved from the beginning and it becomes more accessible☺️ 
 I moved in in the summertime, which might be relevant to note. 
 
 My terrace is leaking and it keeps us from meeting in our shared space or make it cosy. I don’t know if this is something we can reach out to you about, or the community created fund | Måned: Nov | År: 2025 | Landsby: Refshaleøen | Kildeark: Nov 2025

Suddenly I’d walk past a big put lock dinner that I hadn’t heard of, which left me feeling uninvited. I have slowly found my way, but perhaps some other event on top of board game nights to include people when they move in, could be an idea. So that people feel involved from the beginning and it becomes more accessible☺️ 
 I moved in in the summertime, which might be relevant to note.

nodes.combined_text:
Spørgsmål: You've almost made it! Is there anything else you'd like to tell us? | Svar: Again, I get that it's mostly out of your control, and we're all part of a "community" where people have different perspectives, so I'm sure some people might complain about the opposite. But to be honest, the noise complaints this summer (or just in general) have been a bit much. I totally understand that some people want peace and quiet, but they also need to realize they live in a student accommodation. There are a lot of young people here who want to have fun, meet others, and enjoy their student life. Compared to other student accommodations or kollegiums, we're actually pretty quiet and don't have that many events.
 
 So it's frustrating that the few times we do want to do something fun, people start complaining. Like, even during the village festival, which was a community event, people were already asking on the Facebook group when the music was ending just after 10pm...
 
 And all the complaints about BaneGaarden. What else were people expecting from living right next to an event venue? Instead of complaining all the time, it would be better if we found a way to work with BaneGaarden, like Village Reffen did with all the parties and festivals going on in the area. Maybe we could get discounts or something when they have events.
 
 In the end, there aren’t that many loud nights in the village compared to the quiet ones. It would be nice if some people understood that balance and accepted that student life involves having fun, meeting new people, and getting to know your neighbors. | Måned: Sep | År: 2024 | Landsby: Vesterbro | Kildeark: Sep 2024
nodes.Answer:
Again, I get that it's mostly out of your control, and we're all part of a "community" where people have different perspectives, so I'm sure some people might complain about the opposite. But to be honest, the noise complaints this summer (or just in general) have been a bit much. I totally understand that some people want peace and quiet, but they also need to realize they live in a student accommodation. There are a lot of young people here who want to have fun, meet others, and enjoy their student life. Compared to other student accommodations or kollegiums, we're actually pretty quiet and don't have that many events.
 
 So it's frustrating that the few times we do want to do something fun, people start complaining. Like, even during the village festival, which was a community event, people were already asking on the Facebook group when the music was ending just after 10pm...
 
 And all the complaints about BaneGaarden. What else were people expecting from living right next to an event venue? Instead of complaining all the time, it would be better if we found a way to work with BaneGaarden, like Village Reffen did with all the parties and festivals going on in the area. Maybe we could get discounts or something when they have events.
 
 In the end, there aren’t that many loud nights in the village compared to the quiet ones. It would be nice if some people understood that balance and accepted that student life involves having fun, meeting new people, and getting to know your neighbors.
